order: versions ABC in even rounds and CBA in odd rounds, engines default/full then full/default; one fresh process per version, engine and part

method.recalculation: each row builds its fixture untimed, runs 3 warm-up edits of A1, then 3 samples that repeat the edit until 50 ms (at least 3 edits) and record the mean per edit; every sample checks the recalculated value

rows.description: 100,000 formulas =$A$1+n; the edit recalculates all of them
a 64-cell chain =A(n-1)+1 down column A (the benchmark's deepest linear-chain row)
32 levels of B/C branches joined in D (96 formulas, the benchmark's diamond-edit row)
10,000 formulas over distinct ten-row ranges; the edit reaches one
100,000 independent B/C pairs (200,000 formulas); the edit reaches one pair

method.memory: process RSS around loading 100,000 formulas =An+1 into a 100,000-row store (in 10,000-formula transactions), with a forced GC before and after; retained = RSS after minus RSS before; peak = the highest RSS during the load (sampled every millisecond on a worker thread, or the kernel max RSS when the load raised it) minus RSS before
method.xlsx: 50,000 rows x 6 columns (2 text, 2 number, 2 formula columns, 100,000 formulas). Export: toXlsxWorkbook(store.exportSnapshot()). Import: fromXlsxWorkbook(bytes) plus SheetwriteStore.fromSnapshot, of one file written by 0.5.4 for every version. 1 warm-up and 3 samples per process, process median
method.sizes: raw and Brotli quality 11 of the engine's .wasm and of the browser entry's JS import closure
method.aaSpread: largest |1 - median(ABC rounds) / median(CBA rounds)| over versions and engines, per metric
